novelty_basis: The individual identities for the direct (A (x) B) and strong ((A+I) (x) (B+I)) products are classical and the co-normal one follows by complementation; we found no statement classifying the local products with such a linearisation, nor the symmetric-difference case in general (four web searches 2026-10-18, see CLM-C14-06). Small result; possibly folklore.
proof_check: written case analysis (proofs/paper/C14.md Theorem 4); polynomial system solved over C by sympy for all 256 codes (EXP-C14-03); Lean kernel computation for values in {-1,0,1} (character_codes); numerical matrix checks on random graphs
statement:
There is c = (cE, cA, cN) in C^3 with cA != cN and M_c(G*H) = M_c(G) (x) M_c(H) for all graphs, where
M_c(G) = cE I + cA A + cN (J - I - A), exactly for: direct (c = (0,1,0), M = A), code 127 (0,0,1),
strong (1,1,0), co-normal (1,0,1), symmetric difference (1,-1,1), M = S(G) + I with S the Seidel matrix,
and code 141 (1,1,-1), M = I - S(G); the character is unique in each case, and every such product is
associative and commutative.
title: Exactly six local products are Kronecker products in disguise (multiplicative characters)
